title: Knowledge Mycelium
definition: A metaphorical representation of knowledge as a network of interconnected nodes, similar to the mycelium of a mushroom.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine your knowledge as a big, tangled web. Each piece of information is a node connected to other related ideas. This web allows you to easily see how different concepts are interconnected, just like a mushroom's mycelium network helps it absorb nutrients from the soil.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Knowledge mycelium is a conceptual model that visualizes knowledge as a network of interconnected nodes. It's inspired by the intricate network of mycelium in a mushroom, which enables efficient resource acquisition and information sharing. In the context of CADMIES, it helps understand the relationships and evolution of scientific concepts.
difficulty_levels.expert: The knowledge mycelium metaphor is a novel application of network theory in the philosophy of science. It extends the metaphor of the scientific community as a social network to include the interconnectedness of scientific concepts. This view highlights the dynamic, evolving nature of knowledge, and its potential to be understood and navigated through graph theory. It also draws connections to other fields such as social network analysis, complex systems, and emergent properties.

extra_fields.insight: CADMIES' mycelium map visualization helps discover unexpected connections and see the shape of one's knowledge ecosystem.
